newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary sees cut in $350mln Aug loan's price - C.Bnk.
newsitem.headline: Hungary sees cut in $350mln Aug loan's price - C.Bnk.

text.p: The National Bank of Hungary said on Friday that it was renegotiating the terms of a $350 million syndicated loan it took up in August as the assessment of the Hungarian economy substantially improved abroad.
"We renegotiate the price (of the loan) and we will do a very substantial cut in the price," NBH vice president Frigyes Harshegyi told Reuters.
The loan was priced 50 bps over LIBOR. Harshegyi said the size of the price cut Hungary was likely to reach, was some "tens of basis points".

Hungary received an investment grade rating for the first time from one of the world's two most influential credit rating agencies, in October. Standard $ Poor's raised the country's foreign currency debt rating to BBB-minus.
Harshegyi denied reports from a London banker, who told Reuters earlier on Friday that Hungary was seeking a new $350 million loan to refinance the August loan with a lower-priced credit.

"We are so stuffed with money and the current account is so good, that we do not need loans not only this year, but next year either, and, I think, not even in 1998 if the economy advances at the present pace," he said.
Harshegyi added that Hungary's financial position had improved so much in 1996 that the country will repay loans of $1 billion ahead of maturity, in the next few months.
Part of the $1 billion was the $200 million which Hungary repaid to the International Monetary Fund (IMF) earlier on Friday, Harshegyi said.
The country will repay further $200 million to the World Bank early next year, he added.
Hungary will also repay 750 million marks, which it took up in 1988-1989 with German government guarantee, as well as other smaller loans it took up in 1990-1991, Hershegyi added.
